terrain.art: bridge hex, also the British exit hex

objectives.note: British exit hex (outlined in red on the map), also the River Coa bridge. Any ordered Anglo-Portuguese unit of any strength leaving the board by this hex scores one banner for BR; leaders do not score (survey 006). Anglo-Portuguese units cannot retreat off the bridge; a unit that cannot retreat takes one block of damage per hex it could not move. OPEN RULINGS QUESTION (survey): the text gives the French one banner if an Anglo-Portuguese unit is eliminated on this hex; it is not stated whether that is one banner in total for the unit or an extra on top of the normal kill banner. Not decided here.

notes: River Coa: 6 hexes in one piece: 0,1 0,2 0,3 0,4 (bridge) 1,0 2,0. It is impassable except at the bridge (survey). The bridge hex 0,4 is also the exit objective; the river art enters 0,4 from the left and leaves through the top edge.

Fieldworks 2,4 and 2,5 are flat (on plain): scan.py reports hill 0.15 and 0.10 there, but that is the dark shadow of the brown works, not hill rays (no ray ring in the plain crop; survey gives 9 hills and flat entrenchments). Works are three-sided: 2,4 has a wall on W, SW and SE (open to the E); 2,5 on SW, SE and E (open to the W). A PT/LT (brown block) stands on each.

Almeida: two hexes 0,11 (BR/FA on it) and 0,12, both recorded as fortress (survey: two town hexes, treated as town, ignore one flag for BR and PT). The windmill hex 4,10 shows a windmill and a few houses on a pale ground; recorded as windmill.
Hills: 0,5 (under the Craufurd block), 2,7 2,8 2,9 3,9, 6,0 7,0, 8,4 8,5 (under HC blocks); the survey count of 9 matches. Forests: 0,6 and 5,0.

Survey discrepancy 6: no Ney block on the map; the French leaders are Ferey (6,2 with FR/LN), Loison (6,6, alone) and Mermet (8,9 with FR/LN). British: Craufurd (0,5, alone), Anson (0,9 with BR/HC), Sydney (2,3 with BR/LN; may be Sydenham). No Portuguese leader. PT/LT 2 (brown blocks) both on the entrenchments.
